id.description: the provider's id for it, echoed in the result

args.description: its arguments: the object the tool's input schema describes

source.description: optional: the request or other entity this call came from

result.description: What a tool returned, and how long the call took.

ms.description: how long the tool took, in milliseconds

call.description: the call it is the result of

output.description: What produced the text beside it: the request, for a model’s own output, or the call whose failure is being reported. Only output carries it — text a person or a system wrote has none.

id.description: the provider's id for this piece of output, as `call.id` is its id for the call — what a later revision of the same item is matched on

value.description: the same output as data, for a reader that parses rather than reads: a tool that declares an outputSchema answers its structured content here, beside the text a person reads

refusal.description: A deliberate no: the tool or provider refused the request. Never tracked; its prose is on the content component beside it.

code.description: the tool or provider's reason for refusing

exception.description: A failure the code did not expect, whoever caused it: a defect report, not a stop. On its own, its message is on the `content` component beside it; these properties are filled in by whichever process caught the error, and by nobody else.

stack.description: the stack trace, as the runtime reported it

request.description: what was being served when it threw

request_id.description: the id returned to the caller and tagged in Sentry

execution.description: Who holds a recorded tool invocation; its state is computed from the interruption mark and explicitly named answers.

state.description: The lifecycle derived from its interruption mark, holder and recorded answers.

by.description: the server or process running it

tool.description: A registered tool that callers can invoke.

name.description: what callers call it; the entity id is derived from it

revision.description: implementation revision used by builders to detect changed code

call_ready.description: a call nobody has claimed and nobody scheduled: run the tool it names and attach the result. A call written already claimed (the caller runs it) owes nothing

call_woken.description: a scheduled call whose wake has fired and that nobody has run yet: run it now. Never matches in a graph that does not load the wake components, where `call_ready` alone applies and every call is due when it is written

finding.description: What a check measured: fail for a violated contract, warn for a leak or a verdict it could not establish.
